sections.skill: Organize folders and name files so they sort and search well

questions.prompt: Which file name sorts best by date?
questions.intro: Records you cannot find are almost as bad as no records. Use a simple FOLDER STRUCTURE, for example by year, then by type: 2026 / Receipts, 2026 / Invoices, 2026 / Contracts, 2026 / Tax. Use consistent FILE NAMES that sort well, with the date first in year-month-day order: "2026-03-14 Invoice 104 Lopez.pdf." Keep originals and important signed documents, and store backups separately. A few minutes of naming now saves hours of searching later.

questions.prompt: Unlabeled jars are like what?
questions.intro: Imagine a kitchen where every jar is unlabeled. Finding the sugar means opening each jar. Labeled jars, arranged by type on shelves, make it quick. Digital files work the same way: folders are the shelves and file names are the labels. A clear label that starts with the date is like writing "packed March 2026" on a jar.
